parts.problem_md:
An organisation has decided to use video-conferencing for its meetings.

**State **the hardware and software required to set up the video-conference.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of the hardware and software required to set up the video-conference include:

Max **three **of the following:

**Hardware**

- Camera **[1 mark]**
- Monitor **[1 mark]**
- Microphone **[1 mark]**
- Speakers **[1 mark]**
- Router **[1 mark]**

Max **three **of the following:

**Software**

- Software/hardware drivers **[1 mark]**
- Video conferencing software **[1 mark]**
- CODEC **[1 mark]**
- Echo cancelling software **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A student is able to access a secure area of the school’s website using zero login.

**Explain **what is meant by zero login.
parts.solution_md:
A zero login can be explained as:

Any **two **of the following:

- It is a security method to protect the resources/data that the user can access **[1 mark]**
- It is an authentication method **[1 mark]**
- Ability to pass through security information from initial login to host PC **[1 mark]**
- It requires no manual input from the user **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Discuss **the advantages and disadvantages of using web-conferencing rather than video-conferencing for meetings.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of advantages and disadvantages of using web-conferencing rather than video-conferencing for meetings include:

Max **four **of the following:

**Advantages**

- Reduced cost as less extra hardware/dedicated software is needed **[1 mark]**
- Far simpler interface for employees **[1 mark]**
- Fewer issues with lip sync/video lag/buffering **[1 mark]**
- Can be used on more devices **[1 mark]**
- Increased privacy as there is no camera **[1 mark]**
- More flexibility for the employee as they do not need to be in front of a camera **[1 mark]**

Max **four **of the following:

**Disadvantages**

- Requires internet connection and it must be stable/reliable **[1 mark]**
- Cannot see the body language of the people in the conference **[1 mark]**
- Cannot tell if the employees are paying attention/or even there **[1 mark]**
- Fewer features than video-conferencing **[1 mark]**
- Less personal as you cannot see the person **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
One of the risks when entering a password into a computer system is key logging.

Give **two** security improvements that could be made to prevent key logging.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of security improvements that could be made include:

Any **two **of the following:

- Install anti-keylogging/anti-malware/anti-spyware software **[1 mark]**
- Check the computer system before entering confidential data **[1 mark]**
- Update the computer system regularly **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: State, **giving a reason** for your choice, the hardware required to set up an electronic conference.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of the hardware required to set up an electronic conference include:

Max **three **for any of the following devices:

- Computer/smartphone **[1 mark]**
- Camera/webcam **[1 mark]**
- Monitors **[1 mark]**
- Microphone **[1 mark]**
- Speaker/headphones **[1 mark]**
- Router **[1 mark]**

Plus **max two** for any of the linked reasons:

** Computer/smartphone**

- to connect the peripherals used in the conference **[1 mark]**

**Camera/webcam**

- to capture moving images of the conference/participants **[1 mark]**

**Monitors**

- to view the participants/contents/web page of the conference **[1 mark]**

**Microphone**

- to capture the audio of the conference/participants **[1 mark]**

**Speaker/headphones**

- so participants can listen to others in the conference **[1 mark]**

**Router**

- to connect to the internet **[1 mark]**

**Electronic conferencing can be explained as:**

**Any two of the following:**

- This is a communication system **[1 mark]**
- A structured discussion between two or more people **[1 mark]**
- This is carried out virtually/online/over the internet **[1 mark]**
- Involves video, web and audio **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Many organisations use audio-conferencing or video-conferencing as some employees work from home.

**Discuss **the advantages and disadvantages of using audio-conferencing rather than video-conferencing.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of advantages and disadvantages of using audio-conferencing rather than video-conferencing include:

Max **five **of the following:

**Advantages**

- Simpler interface for employees **[1 mark]**
- Less equipment is required therefore it is cheaper **[1 mark]**
- More flexibility/can dress casually for the employee as they do not need to be in front of a camera **[1 mark]**
- No issues with lip sync **[1 mark]**
- Can do other tasks as there is no camera/cannot be seen **[1 mark]**
- More privacy as the viewers cannot see inside your home/office **[1 mark]**

**AND/OR**

Max **five **of the following:

**Disadvantages**

- Doesn’t let you have visual aids during calls **[1 mark]**
- Cannot see the body language of the people in the conference **[1 mark]**
- Cannot tell if the employees are paying attention **[1 mark]**
- Fewer features than video-conferencing **[1 mark]**
- Less personal as you cannot see the person **[1 mark]**
- Harder to control the meeting as you do not know who is speaking next **[1 mark]**
- Ask ChatGPT **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A systems analyst has been asked to carry out an analysis of a company’s current computer system.

Members of the team can use video-conferencing to join business meetings from different locations around the world.

**Describe**, giving reasons, **three **disadvantages of using video-conferencing for business meetings rather than meeting in person.
parts.solution_md:
One disadvantage of using video-conferencing for business meetings is that it **requires a fast and reliable internet connection**. If the connection is weak, **documents and images may take longer to load**, or participants may **experience lag and audio delays**, making communication difficult.

Another issue is that** time zone differences can make scheduling difficult**, especially when **employees are in different parts of the world**. This can lead to meetings being held at inconvenient times for some participants, reducing productivity.

Additionally, video-conferencing may **require specialist hardware and software**, which **can be expensive for companies to purchase and maintain**. Businesses may also need to invest in training staff to use the system effectively, which takes time and resources.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Three **matched **pairs:
> 
> - Requires a good/fast/reliable internet connection → documents/images may require more bandwidth **[2 marks]**
> - Time zone differences → staff work in other parts of the world/time of meeting may be difficult **[2 marks]**
> - Requires specialist hardware/software → can be expensive to purchase **[2 marks]**
> 
> **[Total marks: 6/6]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 6-mark "describe" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **Use a clear structure with matched pairs**
> 
>   1. Each disadvantage should be followed by a reason/explanation.
>   2. Example: "Time zone differences can make scheduling difficult, as staff work in different parts of the world."
> 2. **Avoid vague or one-word answers**
> 
>   1. Instead of just saying "internet issues", explain "a slow or unstable internet connection can cause delays, affecting communication."
> 3. **Use business-related terminology where possible**
> 
>   1. Terms like "bandwidth," "productivity," "specialist hardware," and "real-time communication" demonstrate a stronger understanding of the topic.
> 4. **Prioritise practical challenges businesses face**
> 
>   1. Think about real-world workplace issues, such as team collaboration, costs, and technical difficulties.
> 5. **Check that each point is unique**
> 
>   1. Avoid writing two points that overlap too much (e.g., "internet connection issues" and "disconnection issues" could be too similar).

parts.problem_md:
A student has set up a password for his laptop computer. The password he has chosen is Px2zY!Cg3?bd

**Discuss **the benefits and drawbacks of using this password.
parts.solution_md:
The student’s password Px2zY!Cg3?bd is **strong and secure** because it is long and contains a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, making it **harder to crack** using brute force attacks. Additionally, it **does not contain personal information, which reduces the risk of someone guessing it**. The password’s** length also makes shoulder surfing more difficult**, as it is harder for someone nearby to memorise.

However, the **complexity of the password makes it difficult to remember,** which could lead to the **user writing it down, increasing the risk of unauthorised access**. The **mix of letters, numbers, and symbols may also cause confusion**, such as mistaking ‘2’ for ‘Z’ or ‘1’ for ‘I’, making it **easier to mistype**. Additionally, the user may need to look at the keyboard while typing, slowing down the login process.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> To gain full marks you **must **have correct answers for both benefits and drawbacks
> 
> - Strong password that is hard to crack **[1 mark]**
> - More secure as it does not contain personal information **[1 mark]**
> - Longer password reduces the risk of shoulder surfing **[1 mark]**
> - Difficult to remember due to complexity **[1 mark]**
> - May need to be written down, increasing security risks **[1 mark]**
> - Letters and numbers may be confused, leading to typing errors **[1 mark]**
> 
> **[Total marks: 6/6]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 6-mark "Discuss" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **Include both benefits and drawbacks**
> 
>   1. The mark scheme requires both positive and negative aspects, so make sure to balance your answer.
> 2. **Be specific about security advantages**
> 
>   1. Instead of saying "it is secure," explain why: "It includes a mix of characters, making brute force attacks more difficult."
> 3. **Consider real-world usability issues**
> 
>   1. Mention practical problems, such as difficulty remembering the password or the need to look at the keyboard while typing.
> 4. **Use comparative phrases to strengthen the discussion**
> 
>   1. Example: "Although the password is strong, its complexity may lead to the user writing it down, reducing security."
>   2. This links the benefits and drawbacks, showing a balanced discussion.
> 5. **Avoid vague points and repetition**
> 
>   1. Instead of "it is hard to remember," specify why: "Its combination of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols makes it harder to memorise."
>   2. Cover distinct issues instead of repeating the same idea in different words.

parts.problem_md:
Keeping data secure is very important in any computer system. Many organisations use encryption when sending data.

Another way of protecting data in a computer system is to use passwords.

**Identify **methods to prevent hackers from gaining knowledge of someone’s password.
parts.solution_md:
Methods to prevent hackers from gaining knowledge of someone's password include:

Any **four **of the following:

- Use anti-spyware to prevent key logging **[1 mark]**
- Change passwords regularly **OR **Do not repeat the same password **[1 mark]**
- Use a different password for each system **[1 mark]**
- Avoid common/predictable patterns as they are easier to guess **[1 mark]**
- Use longer passwords as they are harder to guess **[1 mark]**
- Use strong passwords Use two-factor authentication so that hackers need both parts **[1 mark]**
- Use a dropdown list for password entry **[1 mark]**
- Use a biometric password **[1 mark]**
- Do not use passwords that directly links to the user **[1 mark]**
- Do not allow webpages/device to remember the password **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Many young people play online games.

One problem with online gaming is that it is easy to give out personal details accidentally. Some users create weak passwords which could lead to their personal details being accessed.

**Write **down **three **rules that should be applied when setting a strong password.
parts.solution_md:
Example of the rules that should be applied when setting a strong password include:

Any **three **of the following:

- Password should not relate to personal details **[1 mark]**
- Should be a long password **[1 mark]**
- Not previously used password **[1 mark]**
- Should not include repeating/obvious patterns **OR** predictable words **[1 mark]**
- Password should be strong **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:

A technician is setting up the hardware for the video-conference.

**State three **tasks the technician would need to do to set up the hardware for the videoconference.

You **can **assume that the hardware required has already been purchased.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of tasks the technician would need to do to set up the hardware includes:

Any **three **of the following:

- Ensure the video camera/webcam, microphone, speakers/headphones are switched on **[1 mark]**
- Ensure the hardware devices are connected **[1 mark]**
- Carry out tests on the microphone, video camera/webcam and speakers/ headphones **[1 mark]**
- Adjust the video camera/webcam so the headteacher can be seen **[1 mark]**
- Check the volume levels **[1 mark]**
- Check internet connectivity **[1 mark]**
